verdict_text:
NO

The merge takes the second task vector against an already-modified base: after computing `tmp = base + λ(ft1 - base)`, it adds `λ * (ft2 - tmp)` instead of `λ * (ft2 - base)`. This violates "Required result" step 2, which requires `out[X] = base[X] + λ(ft1[X] - base[X]) + λ(ft2[X] - base[X])` with both task vectors measured against the unmodified base, exactly the ordering hazard the specification calls out. The result equals `base + λ(1-λ)(ft1 - base) + λ(ft2 - base)`, so the ft1 contribution is scaled by 0.24 instead of 0.4, which exceeds the 1e-3 relative Frobenius tolerance on the 64 merged tensors. A secondary weakness is that all required checks are plain `assert` statements, which are silently stripped under `python -O`, so they do not reliably "fail loudly" as the "Required checks" section demands.
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
